rule_level_problems.problem: Trigger is (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Discoloration of skin" "finding")), which is not one of the listed common symptoms or warning signs; the task only runs if that finding is recorded somewhere. Yellow skin is a child of Discoloration of skin, so a recorded Yellow skin would trigger it, but the dark/light/absent branches depend on the nurse recording the parent concept.

summary: The red box is encoded faithfully as an Urgent priority (and jaundice (or ...)) with all nine representable criteria present and correctly qualified; the only red-box gap is the Hb threshold, which the language cannot express and the rules drop without a placeholder. The most consequential structural issue is that (clinical_finding Jaundice) is used as priority evidence and task trigger but never checked for, which the house test will flag unless Jaundice is a shared warning sign. All five 'X likely' diagnoses (jaundice, venous stasis, melasma, tinea versicolor, vitiligo, albinism) are correct probable rules following the flowchart; the page's definite 'acute hepatitis A' conclusion from a positive IgM has no rule and may not be representable.
